To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The observed variability is related to the alongshore non-unormity of sandbar features; (2) the alongshore nonuniform sandbar features are related to alongshore non-unform features in the wave field; (3) the alongshore length and the cross-shore amplitude of the nonuniform sandbar feature are related to the along-shore length and the crossshore width of the nonuniform wave feature, respectively.

(i) the observed alongshore nonuniform features are related to the alongshore variability in the wave power, (ii) they are characterized by alongshore lengths of Oð1 kmÞ and lifetimes in months, and (iii) they are governed by free behaviour, that is, they do not respond to variations in the forcing of the wave power, but rather they are forced by the wave power itself.

the nearshore sandbar behaviour is governed by free processes rather than by the prevailing wave conditions and that the observed variability is mostly related to changes in plan shape of quasyrhythmic alongshore sandbar features rather than changes in the bar amplitude.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the observed alongshore non uniform features had lifetimes in the range of months, considerably larger than the characteristic time scales of individual wave events, and that the observed transitions from one alongshore feature to another were gradual and did not always occur during high-energy wave conditions.
alongshore variability of sandbars can be very persistent and that the alongshore variability of the bars is not necessarily related to wave conditions.
the alongshore non-unformity of the sandbar is governed by free behavior rather than by the forcing of the wave conditions.
